Every selected minimal face is proper because its mass is Q<M. A proper inclusion of faces adds a lattice vertex of positive mass, so the selected faces form an antichain. For a strict midpoint the minimal face is the smallest face containing both original faces. Hence same-parity witnesses for distinct faces would force a selected face of mass greater than Q.

The parity count gives at most k selected faces and union mass at most kQ<M. Choosing one interior center per vertex and interpolating on the simplices agrees on their intersections. A Minkowski combination of small interior balls proves the interpolants are actual interior marks, including on common subfaces.

Every positive-weight input into a target on a selected face lies on that same face. Affineness of the centers and a common contraction factor therefore preserve every anchored inclusion there. For targets outside the union, nesting of the contracted inputs suffices. Lattice completeness preserves the exact census.

A pure-base exposing cap controls every new mark on a selected face by rQ, even after buffer renormalization. The specified scalar restores the new weighted geometric mean and tends to one. The matched-mark estimate controls the finitely many outside fiber maxima under the actual moving M, Σ and energy, keeping them below rQ for small t.

The denominator is M−M_U(1−r), and r/[M−M_U(1−r)]<1/M follows from (1−r)(M−M_U)>0. For deficient base rank, integer linear forms with common kernel equal to the base direction span force a sufficiently small perpendicular thickening to have zero transverse displacement at every integer base.
